peopleAlsoAsk.question: What kind of virus is Newcastle disease?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Newcastle disease (ND) is a highly contagious and often severe disease found worldwide that affects birds including domestic poultry. It is caused by virulent strains of avian paramyxovirus type 1.
peopleAlsoAsk.title: Newcastle disease - WOAH - World Organisation for Animal Health

peopleAlsoAsk.question: Can you cure Newcastle disease?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: There is no treatment for Newcastle disease, and, in many countries, infected and susceptible birds in the vicinity of an outbreak are culled to contain transmission of the disease. Prevention is accomplished through vaccination and strict biosecurity.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What is the Newcastle disease vaccine used for?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Newcastle Disease Vaccine, B1 Type, LaSota Strain, has been shown to be effective for the vaccination of healthy chickens 1 day, 2 weeks or 4 weeks of age and older against Newcastle Disease.
